name: Triple whammy
effect: ACE inhibitor or ARB plus a diuretic plus an NSAID markedly increases the risk of acute kidney injury
recommendation: Pharmacist/clinician review: avoid the NSAID where possible and monitor kidney function
source: Lapi F et al. BMJ 2013;346:e8525; STOPP/START v3

name: Anticoagulant + antiplatelet + NSAID
effect: Three drugs that each impair haemostasis: very high risk of major bleeding
recommendation: Escalate for prescriber review before the next dose
source: FDA labels: warfarin / DOACs (Drug Interactions); AGS Beers Criteria 2023

name: Three or more CNS-active drugs
effect: Three or more CNS-active drugs (antidepressants antipsychotics benzodiazepines Z-drugs opioids antiepileptics) increase the risk of falls and fractures in older adults
recommendation: Pharmacist/clinician review: consider reducing the number of CNS-active drugs
source: AGS Beers Criteria 2023 (drug-drug interactions to avoid)

name: Two or more strongly anticholinergic drugs
effect: Cumulative anticholinergic burden increases the risk of confusion delirium constipation and urinary retention in older adults
recommendation: Review whether each anticholinergic drug is still needed
